label: thm-suff
statement: Under the Rasch model with local independence, r_p is sufficient for theta_p and c_i for beta_i
source_locator: secs. 2.4.1 and 2.4.3; direct attribution to Debelak et al. (2022), not Andersen (1970)

label: prp-nosuff
statement: Conditional on fixed known discriminations, the weighted score sum_i lambda_i u_pi is sufficient for theta_p. When lambda is unknown, that parameter-indexed expression is not a statistic and therefore cannot supply a parameter-free Rasch-style conditioning statistic.
source_locator: elementary factorization and definition of a statistic; no originality claim

label: def-ident
statement: A parameter is identified iff the map from parameter to sampling distribution is injective

label: prp-location
statement: Location indeterminacy: (theta_p + c, beta_i + c) is observationally equivalent to (theta_p, beta_i)
source_locator: elementary inline algebra; no originality claim

label: prp-scale
statement: Scale indeterminacy under the 2PL and its absence under the Rasch model
source_locator: elementary inline algebra; no originality claim. Consistent with San Martin (2016, Table 8.1)

label: thm-equiv-fixed
statement: In the fixed-effects Rasch likelihood, item anchoring, item centering, and realized-person centering each select one representative of the same joint location orbit and preserve fitted probabilities and within-type differences.
source_locator: elementary orbit algebra; no originality claim; fixed-effects scope

label: thm-equiv-random
statement: In the marginal Rasch model, shifting item difficulties and translating G together preserves the response distribution; item anchoring, item centering, or a shift-equivariant location constraint on G can select a representative, but realized-person centering is not a marginal-parameter constraint.
source_locator: change-of-variable proof; no originality claim; random-effects scope

label: thm-neyman-scott
statement: JML is inconsistent for fixed I as P grows; in the two-item Rasch case the estimated difficulty difference converges a.s. to twice its true value. Consistent if I also grows with log(I)/P -> 0
source_locator: sec. 9.2.1 (pp. ~152-154), reporting Andersen (1973, pp. 66-69)

label: thm-warm
statement: With known item parameters and Warm's boundedness, smoothness, and replicated-item asymptotic conditions, the WLE with d log w/d theta = J/(2 J-info) has bias o(I^-1), is asymptotically normal, and has the same first-order asymptotic variance as ML.
source_locator: eqs. (6)-(10) and theorem, pp. 430-432; Appendix assumptions and separate variance proof, pp. 444-448

label: prp-plugin
statement: For an independent calibration sample with item covariance V_beta, a regular plug-in ability estimator has variance approximately J-info^-1 + g_beta' V_beta g_beta, where g_beta is its implicit-function sensitivity. With calibration/scoring overlap, cross-covariance terms require a joint sandwich, bootstrap, or joint posterior.
source_locator: first-order implicit-function/delta-method derivation; no magnitude claim from scoring-sample P alone

label: prp-msem-jensen
statement: RMSEM exceeds the mean local standard error by Jensen's inequality, with equality only if the error curve is flat
source_locator: elementary concavity argument; no originality claim

label: prp-mean-weight
statement: The mean normal-normal shrinkage weight is at least w-bar, with equality iff the conditional error variances are constant
source_locator: elementary convexity; corresponds to Appendix C draft (C.23)-(C.24); no originality claim

label: prp-separation
statement: Person separation index S = sigma/RMSEM and strata H = (4S+1)/3, under the three-measurement-error convention
source_locator: sec. 5.5; read directly at intake, C-002 and C-003 confirm the manuscript attribution

label: thm-jensen-sandwich
statement: w-bar <= rho_Theta <= rho-tilde, with equality throughout iff test information is G-a.s. constant
source_locator: vignettes/theory-reliability.Rmd Theorem 1 gives only the outer inequality; the placement of rho_Theta between the two and the organized three-term proof are this book's Jensen adaptation

label: prp-cstar
statement: At fixed item count, on an interval where both reliability functionals are continuous and strictly increasing with unique roots, the common discrimination scale calibrated to a target under the MSEM functional is at least that calibrated under average information; monotonicity is not automatic
source_locator: vignettes/theory-reliability.Rmd Corollary 1; the non-monotonicity caveat is the package's own wording and is preserved

label: prp-joint-posterior
statement: The joint posterior factors into level-1 likelihood, level-2 person distribution, level-3 item prior and level-4 hyperprior
source_locator: ch. 2 sec. 2.1 eqs. 2.1-2.2 give the person/item conditional-independence factorizations; adapted here to the four-level centered-item model

label: prp-centered-item
statement: The mean-centered item prior induced from iid Gaussian auxiliaries is a singular Gaussian of rank I-1 with Var(beta_i)=sigma2(1-1/I), Cov=-sigma2/I and Cor=-1/(I-1)
source_locator: elementary linear algebra on the centering matrix; checked numerically; no originality claim

label: thm-eap-shrinkage
statement: Under the normal working likelihood and a Gaussian prior the posterior is Gaussian with mean w_p theta-hat + (1-w_p) mu and variance (J + 1/sigma2)^-1
source_locator: sec. 2.1 Gaussian compound model; adapted to the IRT normal-working likelihood and proved inline by completing the square

label: prp-underdispersion
statement: For any G and likelihood the posterior-mean ensemble has variance sigma2 minus expected posterior variance; under the constant-error working model it is exactly w-bar times sigma2, while the ML ensemble has variance sigma2 plus MSEM
source_locator: sec. 2.1 gives the Gaussian ensemble under-dispersion and moment repair; the general law-of-total-variance identity and constant-error specialization are proved inline

label: prp-rank-inconsistency
statement: Ranking posterior means need not minimize rank loss in general; when the person posteriors are stochastically ordered, however, posterior-mean, expected-rank, and modal-rank procedures induce the same ordering. Fixed-item Rasch scores satisfy that exception, as do fixed-known-discrimination 2PL weighted scores.
source_locator: sec. 1 gives the generic warning and Appendix A the stochastic-order exception; Shen and Louis (1998) Theorem 2 corroborates the exception; the Rasch/known-2PL monotone-likelihood-ratio verification is inline

label: prp-sumscore
statement: Two design-specific numerical exhibits show that a normal G can produce a strongly skewed score distribution and that a selected bimodal G can produce a symmetric unimodal score distribution only 0.035 in total variation from the selected normal-G score distribution.
source_locator: exact Poisson-binomial recursion plus 4,001-point fixed-grid quadrature on [-12,12]; the structural dependence of score shape on G and item design is not claimed as original

label: def-dp
statement: The Dirichlet process with parameter a finite non-null measure alpha: every measurable partition has Dirichlet-distributed probabilities
source_locator: secs. 1 and 3; alpha is a MEASURE, whose total mass is the concentration and whose normalization is the base measure

label: thm-stick
statement: Stick-breaking: Beta(1,alpha) sticks with iid base-measure locations give a Dirichlet process
source_locator: sec. 1 construction; Theorems 3.4 and 4.3 for the Dirichlet marginals and conjugacy

label: thm-crp
statement: A Polya sequence's empirical measure converges to a discrete P distributed as Ferguson's DP, and the draws are iid given P; the CRP is that partition structure
source_locator: abstract and sec. 1; the reduction of the restaurant metaphor to this theorem is this book's presentation and answers R2-4b

label: thm-antoniak
statement: P(K_J = k) via unsigned Stirling numbers of the first kind, E[K_J] = alpha{psi(alpha+J) - psi(alpha)}, and K_J sufficient for alpha
source_locator: sec. 4, printed pp. 1160-1163; the digamma closed form is one line from his sum and is verified numerically in V8

label: prp-discrete
statement: A Dirichlet process draw is discrete with probability one
source_locator: immediate from the stick-breaking form; Ferguson sec. 4 gives an independent construction

label: prp-semi-location
statement: The semiparametric Rasch structure (beta, G) is observationally equivalent to (beta + c1, G shifted by c), so location is not identified without a restriction
source_locator: sec. 1 identification problem, adapted with the explicit shift orbit from Appendix F sec. F.2.2

label: prp-semi-scale
statement: The Rasch model has no scale indeterminacy, so one constraint suffices; under the 2PL the indeterminacy becomes one in the scale of G itself
source_locator: secs. 8.4-8.7 and Table 8.1 for the Rasch/2PL scale distinction; Appendix F sec. F.2.3 and inline push-forward extend it to G

label: prp-dpm-constraint
statement: For an ordinary unconstrained DPM, centering the base measure at zero centers the prior expectation of G but does not impose E_G[theta]=0 on every realized G; constrained random measures and draw-wise transformations are separate alternatives.
source_locator: sec. 1 supports the ordinary-base-centering statement; the chapter explicitly does not generalize it to every constrained or transformed nonparametric prior

label: prp-partial-id
statement: With I items the I+1 displayed basic scalar functionals of G are Bayesian-identified iff one item parameter is a.s. constant and at least two items are available; they are Laplace-transform values of a test-tilted G, and full identification needs I to infinity.
source_locator: Theorem 5 and expression (11), not Theorem 3 as the Appendix F draft states (see C-014); Theorem 6 gives the asymptotic conditions; no equivalence with a selected pair's total-variation separation is claimed

label: prp-pm-bayes
statement: The posterior mean is Bayes under weighted squared-error loss; E[WSEL] decomposes into sum w(a-eta)^2 plus the irreducible sum w v
source_locator: sec. 2, read directly; the decomposition including the irreducible posterior-variance term is theirs; source lambda_p is translated to registered v_p under TD-3

label: prp-rank-of-mean
statement: The rank of the posterior mean and the posterior mean of the rank are different functionals; they generally differ in value, while their induced ordering agrees under stochastic ordering
source_locator: sec. 2.1 p. 457 gives the expected-rank action and its generally noninteger values; sec. 3 Theorem 2 p. 459 gives induced-order agreement under stochastic ordering; Goldstein & Spiegelhalter (1996) supplies the rank-uncertainty context

label: thm-incompatible
statement: There exist independent nondegenerate overlapping posteriors for which no trait vector is both WSEL-optimal and carries the ISEL-optimal equal-mass distribution, hence no vector attains those two optima plus the rank-optimal ordering
source_locator: secs. 2.1-2.4 supply the three Bayes actions and Theorem 1's midpoint-quantile ISEL solution; Paddock et al. abstract/sec. 2.1 supplies the general incompatibility motivation; the narrower existence statement and correctly computed normal example are this book's and checked against a frozen table in V8

label: thm-cb
statement: The constrained Bayes estimator uses a = sqrt(1 + H1/H2) to match posterior expected ensemble mean and variance; under posterior independence H1 yields the exact per-unit (1-1/P) specialization
source_locator: Theorem 1 and proof pp. 534-535 give the general rule; Remarks 1-2 give inflation and nonexistence conditions; V8 checks the independent-posterior form, its exact equality to the package expression through R's P-1 sample-variance denominator, and the omitted cross-person covariance term

label: prp-cb-affine
statement: CB is a positive affine map of posterior means, so it preserves their ordering and all defined standardized empirical moments; it cannot change an existing shape mismatch
source_locator: sec. 3 p. 459 states rank invariance; the standardized-moment and shape statements are the book's elementary positive-affine extension

label: thm-gr
statement: The triple-goal estimator uses Gbar midpoint-quantile mass points, discretized posterior ranks, and theta-hat_k = U_{R-hat_k}; exact tied expected ranks require a loss-equivalent within-block permutation rule
source_locator: sec. 2.1 p. 457 gives expected ranks; sec. 2.3 pp. 457-458 gives ISEL and midpoint quantiles; sec. 2.4 pp. 458-459 gives the three-step construction and optimal assignment; uniform randomization within exact tie blocks is the book's exchangeability-preserving completion

label: prp-gr-edf
statement: Every permitted GR assignment is a permutation of the ISEL-optimal mass points and therefore carries G-hat exactly; tied expected-rank blocks admit multiple loss-equivalent permutations
source_locator: sec. 2.4 p. 459; the permutation argument is exact, while the explicit tie-block completion and verification are supplied here

label: prp-gr-regret
statement: General GR regret is K^-1 sum_k (U_{R-hat_k}-eta_k)^2; when GR ranks agree with posterior-mean ranks it simplifies to K^-1 sum_j (U_j-eta_(j))^2
source_locator: sec. 4.2 eq. (14) p. 462 gives the sorted form after adopting posterior-mean ranks, which the source says agree with optimal ranks for a wide class; the book states the actual-permutation identity first and checks both cases in V8

label: prp-rank-reliability
statement: In Lockwood's Gaussian model rank performance depends on tau/sigma; over the book's matched-reliability common-form Rasch grid, the mean reliability effect exceeds the maximum four-shape gap fourfold, while the shape gap has an interior peak and then declines
source_locator: sec. 2 gives the Gaussian statement under its model conditions; the Rasch calculation uses full-support midpoint-quantile quadrature, common-wbar interpolation, a frozen 400-versus-800-node convergence receipt, and a unit-variance logistic heavy-tail working shape in code/R/02-rank-concordance.R and tables/F-rank-reliability-*.rds

label: prp-2pl-pattern-id
statement: With known fixed 2PL item parameters, the observable response-pattern probabilities are at most 2^I-1 independent integral functionals of G; an unrestricted G is not point-identified by a finite test, while a sharp joint characterization with free unknown item parameters remains open
source_locator: finite response alphabet and a K by K+1 null-space construction with K=2^I; no originality claim; the free-item sharp analogue is explicitly not asserted
